heading: INT. MURANO GLASSWORKS - FURNACE HALL - NIGHT

units.text: INT. MURANO GLASSWORKS - FURNACE HALL - NIGHT
The great furnace has burned for four hundred years and has never once gone out.
It breathes orange light across a hall of crooked chandeliers, rows of unsold goblets, and a locked case of Doge's glass behind a velvet rope.
The air is a held breath.
SERAFINA BOLDRINI, 50s, apron, silver braid, tends the furnace with a long iron pipe and the patience of someone who has done so for decades.
She hums an old lullaby.
Across the hall, CHIARA MENEGHEL, 30s, in a borrowed apprentice smock and a coat of nerve, drifts between the chandeliers.
Her gloved hand pauses on a showcase latch.
Her other hand holds a velvet bag.
Chiara, you're late.
units.name: SERAFINA

units.text: The vaporetto, signora.
units.name: CHIARA

units.text: Always the vaporetto.
units.name: SERAFINA

units.text: Chiara lets the latch go.
Crosses to the furnace, ears red with the heat.
She lifts a pipe, gathers a gob of molten glass, and for a moment they work side by side, the older woman correcting the younger's angle with a touch.
Slower. Glass has no patience for those in a hurry.
units.name: SERAFINA

units.text: I'll remember.
units.name: CHIARA

units.text: You won't. But it's kind of you to say.
units.name: SERAFINA

units.text: The glass glows like a small sun.
Chiara turns it, gently, and the lullaby seems to hum itself in her throat.
She is, for the first time, perfectly calm.
She lifts her eyes to the case.
Back to the glass.
Then, softly:
It's very beautiful, what you do.
units.name: CHIARA

units.text: It is.
units.name: SERAFINA

units.text: Serafina smiles.
She sets down her pipe.
Reaches into her apron pocket and draws out a long, cold key.
Holds it in her palm.
My daughter used to say the same. The last night she worked here, she asked me to open the case.
units.name: SERAFINA

units.text: She steps toward the Doge's glass.
Chiara goes rigid.
She was a very good thief. Very patient. Not patient enough.
units.name: SERAFINA

units.text: She slips the key in the lock.
The case swings open on empty velvet.
Your mother never did learn to wait.
units.name: SERAFINA

units.text: Chiara drops the velvet bag.
Behind her, the furnace roars.
